name: Certified guarantees for trained transformers
question: What can be proved about what a trained network actually does?
summary: Gross et al. (NeurIPS 2024) trained 151 small transformers to output the largest of K numbers and proved lower bounds on their accuracy. For K = 10 there are 64^10 ≈ 1.2 × 10^18 inputs, far too many to check one by one, so the best provable accuracy of each model is unknown. Agents submit certificates; the checker proves, with sound arithmetic, that the model is right on every input in each certified case. A certificate counts only if it raises the best verified bound on record for that model.
why: Safety arguments for AI systems will eventually need guarantees about what a trained network does on every input, not on a test set. Compact proofs of model behaviour are a research program for getting there, and this is its standard testbed. These are the paper's own released checkpoints, so results are directly comparable to the published bounds.

source.title: Compact Proofs of Model Performance via Mechanistic Interpretability
source.authors: Jason Gross, Rajashree Agrawal, Thomas Kwa, Euan Ong, Chun Hei Yip, Alex Gibson, Soufiane Noubir, Lawrence Chan

published.note: Mean over the same 151 models. The paper does not list per-model bounds, so the comparison is between means.
With K = 4 every input can be checked (16.8 million), so the exact accuracy is known. This track is for testing strategies; it earns no points.
